name: Measure the Period of a Pendulum
imageAlt: A pendulum suspended from a laboratory support
description: Measure the period of a pendulum by recording the time required for several oscillations.
purpose: Practice physical measurements and apply error theory to experimental results.
procedure: Set up the pendulum using the stand, string, and sphere.
Measure and record the pendulum length.
Displace the sphere slightly from its equilibrium position and release it.
Measure the time required for several complete oscillations.
Repeat the measurement and calculate the average period.
Compare the measurements and discuss possible sources of experimental error.

name: Experimental Determination of Gravitational Acceleration
imageAlt: A pendulum used to investigate gravitational acceleration
description: Determine gravitational acceleration experimentally by measuring the length and period of a pendulum.
purpose: Calculate gravitational acceleration from experimental measurements and analyze measurement errors.
procedure: Assemble a pendulum and measure its length.
Displace the sphere slightly and release it.
Measure the time required for several complete oscillations.
Repeat the measurements to improve reliability.
Calculate the period using the measured time and number of oscillations.
Use the pendulum length and period to estimate gravitational acceleration.
Compare the experimental result with the accepted value and discuss sources of error.

name: Parallelogram of Forces
imageAlt: Force vectors represented by a parallelogram diagram
description: Investigate the resultant of concurrent forces using the parallelogram method.
purpose: Verify experimentally the parallelogram method for combining forces.
procedure: Set up the apparatus so that the forces act concurrently.
Connect the strings and dynamometers according to the laboratory arrangement.
Record the magnitude and direction of the forces.
Represent the forces as vectors using an appropriate scale.
Construct the parallelogram and determine the resultant graphically.
Compare the graphical result with the experimental arrangement and discuss differences.

name: Potential Block and Tackle
imageAlt: A pulley system used to study mechanical advantage
description: Explore the operation of a potential block-and-tackle system and the relationship between applied force and load.
purpose: Understand the operating principle of a potential pulley system and investigate its mechanical advantage.
procedure: Assemble the pulley system using the available laboratory apparatus.
Attach the load to the moving part of the system.
Apply force through the string and observe the movement of the load.
Measure the applied force using the dynamometer.
Record the load and applied-force measurements.
Compare the applied force with the load and discuss the mechanical advantage.

name: Lever
imageAlt: A lever resting on a fulcrum with loads at different distances
description: Investigate how the position of the fulcrum and the applied force affect the behavior of a lever.
purpose: Understand the basic principle of the lever and the relationship between force and lever arm.
procedure: Place the lever bar on its support.
Position a load at a measured distance from the fulcrum.
Apply force at another point until the lever reaches equilibrium.
Record the load, applied force, and corresponding distances.
Repeat the experiment using different positions.
Compare the results and discuss the principle of moments.

name: Uniform Rectilinear Motion (MRU)
imageAlt: A cart moving along a straight laboratory track
description: Study motion along a straight path and investigate the relationship between distance, time, and constant velocity.
purpose: Verify experimentally the characteristics of uniform rectilinear motion.
procedure: Set up the track and prepare the cart for motion.
Establish several measurement positions along the track.
Release or move the cart under the conditions specified by the laboratory setup.
Record the time taken to reach each position.
Calculate the average velocity for the measured intervals.
Prepare distance-versus-time data and analyze whether the motion is approximately uniform.

name: Uniformly Accelerated Rectilinear Motion (MRUV)
imageAlt: A cart moving along an inclined laboratory track
description: Investigate straight-line motion in which velocity changes over time due to acceleration.
purpose: Study uniformly accelerated motion using experimental measurements of position and time.
procedure: Prepare the track and arrange the apparatus for accelerated motion.
Identify and record the measurement positions.
Release the cart under consistent initial conditions.
Measure the time associated with each position.
Repeat the measurements to check consistency.
Analyze the position and time data to investigate the acceleration.

name: Free Fall
imageAlt: An object falling vertically during a physics experiment
description: Investigate the vertical motion of a falling object and estimate gravitational acceleration.
purpose: Study free-fall motion and experimentally determine the acceleration due to gravity.
procedure: Set up the apparatus in a safe location with a clear falling path.
Measure the vertical distance through which the object will fall.
Release the object from rest according to the apparatus instructions.
Record the fall time using the available timing system.
Repeat the measurement for consistency.
Use the measured distance and time to estimate gravitational acceleration.
Discuss measurement uncertainty and possible experimental errors.

name: Projectile Motion
imageAlt: A ball following a curved projectile trajectory
description: Study the trajectory and horizontal range of a projectile launched at different angles or initial conditions.
purpose: Investigate projectile motion and compare experimental ranges with theoretical predictions.
materials: Projectile launcher or suitable launching apparatus
procedure: Set up the launching apparatus securely.
Measure or set the launch angle according to the experiment instructions.
Launch the projectile and measure its horizontal range.
Repeat the measurement under the same conditions.
Change the launch angle or another specified variable.
Record and compare the measured ranges.
Discuss the relationship between launch conditions and projectile trajectory.

name: Circular Motion
imageAlt: A rotating apparatus used to study circular motion
description: Investigate circular motion and the relationship between angular and linear quantities.
purpose: Study circular motion and determine linear quantities from angular measurements.
procedure: Set up the circular-motion apparatus according to the laboratory instructions.
Measure the radius of the circular path.
Set the object in circular motion.
Measure the time required for a known number of revolutions.
Calculate the period and frequency.
Determine the angular velocity and corresponding linear velocity.
Compare the calculated quantities and discuss the motion.

name: Atwood Machine
imageAlt: Two masses connected by a string over a pulley
description: Study the motion of two connected masses and investigate how their mass difference affects acceleration.
purpose: Apply Newton's laws and verify the relationship between mass distribution and theoretical acceleration.
procedure: Assemble the pulley and suspend the two masses using the string.
Measure and record the masses used in the experiment.
Position the masses so the system can move freely.
Release the system from rest and measure its motion using the available timing method.
Repeat the measurements to improve reliability.
Calculate the theoretical acceleration using the measured masses.
Compare the experimental and theoretical results and discuss possible sources of error.

name: Static and Kinetic Friction on an Inclined Plane
imageAlt: A block resting on an inclined plane
description: Investigate the conditions under which an object begins to slide and continues moving on an inclined plane.
purpose: Determine static and kinetic friction coefficients and study motion on an inclined plane.
materials: Dynamometer, if required by the setup
procedure: Place the object on the inclined plane.
Increase the inclination gradually until the object begins to slide.
Record the angle at which motion begins.
Use the measured angle and the appropriate physical relationship to estimate the static friction coefficient.
Investigate the object while it is sliding using the method specified by the laboratory setup.
Record the required measurements and estimate the kinetic friction coefficient.
Compare the two coefficients and discuss experimental uncertainty.

name: Spring and Elastic Potential Energy
imageAlt: A spring used to investigate elastic deformation
description: Explore the deformation of a spring under an applied load and investigate the relationship between force and extension.
purpose: Proposed activity to investigate spring behavior and elastic potential energy.
procedure: Secure the spring to a suitable support.
Measure and record its initial length.
Apply a load and measure the resulting extension.
Repeat with different loads, staying within the spring's safe elastic range.
Record the applied loads and corresponding extensions.
Plot force against extension and examine the relationship.
Discuss how energy may be stored in the deformed spring.

name: The Loop-the-Loop
imageAlt: A small sphere traveling through a vertical loop track
description: Investigate the minimum release height required for a sphere to complete a vertical loop.
purpose: Study conservation of mechanical energy and compare theoretical predictions with experimental observations.
procedure: Set up the loop track and verify that the apparatus is secure.
Identify the reference point and measure the relevant dimensions of the track.
Release the sphere from a selected height without giving it an additional push.
Observe whether the sphere completes the loop.
Repeat using different release heights.
Determine the lowest tested height at which the sphere completes the loop under the experimental conditions.
Compare the observations with predictions based on conservation of mechanical energy and discuss differences.

name: Angular Impulse and Conservation of Angular Momentum
imageAlt: A person rotating on a stool while changing the position of their arms
description: Observe how changing the distribution of mass around a rotating body affects its rotational motion.
purpose: Observe the conservation of angular momentum when the external torque on a rotating system is negligible.
procedure: Ensure that the rotating platform is stable and the surrounding area is clear.
Following the instructor's safety directions, have a participant sit or stand on the rotating platform while holding a weight in each hand.
Begin rotating at a controlled speed with the arms extended.
Bring the arms closer to the body as instructed.
Observe the change in rotational speed.
Repeat the observation with consistent conditions when safe to do so.
Discuss the observations using the principles of moment of inertia and conservation of angular momentum.
